Hi Markus / Monica,

Thanks again for the kickoff this morning. We ran through high-level requirements with our security team and they asked for:

- VPC peering topology and egress controls
- Details on private endpoint auth & cert rotation
- Expected IP ranges and ASN for the edge appliance
- On-prem package sizing and snapshot/rollback process

Could you confirm the staging window and whether the appliance needs a dedicated subnet (we prefer single /24 for simplicity) or if we can use an existing one?

Best,
Alicia Ramos
Sr. Director, IT Operations
CedarHealth Systems

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Oct 2028 11:05:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Secure Connect: VPC peering & on-prem delivery plan

Hi Alicia — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front:

- Topology: We recommend a dedicated VPC peering connection (cross-account) with explicit route tables. We'll provide CIDR ranges from our edge appliance pool: 10.138.64.0/24 (edge management) and 10.138.65.0/24 (application egress).
- Egress controls: We'll ship a default-deny iptables policy on the appliance and a managed egress policy that can be scoped by security groups at your end.
- Private endpoint auth: Mutual TLS (mTLS) + short-lived tokens. Our rotation process uses the customer's KMS-backed certs when requested; otherwise we manage certs with quarterly rotation.
- Appliance sizing: For your expected sustained qps we recommend a 2-GPU small package (8GB per GPU quantized profile); fallback 1-GPU for staging.
- Subnet: dedicated /24 is cleaner for routing and future NACLs — we strongly prefer that.

I'll attach an implementation checklist and a sample runbook. Proposed staging window: Oct 16-18, 2028 UTC-4 morning (02:00-10:00 UTC) to reduce traffic impact. Does that work?

Markus Klein
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-implementation-checklist.xlsx
